column1: #   The origin is where the row's reading comes from -- `unihan` (derived from
#   the Unihan database), `manual` (curated by hand, which is what every row of
#   this table is), or `corpus` (mined from corpus text). `dictc quality` audits
#   the column so a row's provenance travels with it.
#   The reading is the one the word actually has, spelled as one syllable per
#   character separated by apostrophes. Tone marks, tone digits and an
#   apostrophe-free spelling are accepted as well; dictc folds every form onto
#   the toneless syllable table and asserts that each row reads as exactly one
#   legal syllable per character. A row whose reading is already the word's L3a
#   baseline is a confirmation and changes nothing; a row that names a different
#   reading adds that key and ranks it above the baseline key for the same word.
# The table is a ranking aid, not a correctness source: the readings come from
# the word's own meaning, which is what disambiguates a polyphonic character
# (银行 is yin'hang, not yin'xing). It covers the main compounds of the
# high-frequency polyphonic characters, starting with the ones ADR-0000 names:
# 行 重 长 乐 还 都 得 地 了 着, and then the rest of the common set.
# Rows are derived systematically: every word of data/raw/base.tsv that contains
# one of those characters, with the reading that word has.
# ── common words with a polyphonic character ───────────────────────────────
